findings.evidence: references/naming-conventions.md, "Spelling": `factorization` not `factorisation`. `grep -E '(def|theorem) \w*([Ff]avour|...)' EpsilonEridani/` returns hits only in this new file; the same file uses `Flavor`, `Species.flavorPair`, `FlavorRelation`.
findings.fix: Rename to `favored`/`unfavored` throughout (`favored_add_unfavored`, `favored_eq_apply_quark`, `favored_pion_plus_down_eq_favored_pion_plus_up`, …), keeping "favoured" in docstrings and module prose as the author intends for "flavour".
findings.issue: `favoured`/`unfavoured` are British spellings used in declaration names: `def favoured` (229), `def unfavoured` (235), and the theorems at 241, 245, 251, 257, 262, 270, 286, 302, 318, 334, 381, 389, 397, 406, 483, 491, 501, 604, 610, 616, 622, 643, 652, 662 — 26 declarations in all. The naming document is explicit: "Declaration names use American English spelling" (prose may keep other spellings). The PR itself applies that rule to `Flavor`/`flavorPair`/`FlavorRelation`/`IsValenceFlavor`, so the file is internally inconsistent, and `grep` shows no other British-spelled identifier anywhere in `EpsilonEridani/`.

findings.evidence: Mathlib names exactly this shape with `_iff`: `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/SpinGroup.lean:226` `star_mem_iff : star x ∈ pinGroup Q ↔ x ∈ pinGroup Q`; `Mathlib/GroupTheory/GroupAction/SubMulAction.lean:503` `neg_mem_iff : -x ∈ p ↔ x ∈ p`. The PR already follows this for `IsValenceFlavor.quark_mem_iff`/`antiquark_mem_iff` (Symmetries.lean:146,154).
findings.fix: Rename to `conj_mem_flavorPair_iff` (or `conj_mem_iff`, matching the Mathlib spelling) and `pion_map_swap_mem_valence_conj_iff`.
findings.issue: `conj_mem_flavorPair : s.conj ∈ flavorPair i ↔ s ∈ flavorPair i` is an `Iff` but its name reads as a one-directional membership claim ("the conjugate is in the pair"). Same shape at Symmetries.lean:628, `pion_map_swap_mem_valence_conj`, also an `Iff` named without `_iff`.

summary: Names otherwise describe their conclusions and no notation is introduced, but the new `favoured`/`unfavoured` identifiers use British spelling in violation of the explicit American-spelling rule (and contradict the PR's own `Flavor`/`flavorPair` choice), and two `Iff` lemmas are named as if they were one-directional membership facts.
